- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and underpredicts the next leg — add a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to compensate.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after a peak or rises after a trough), model often lags — shift forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates volatility in the first 7–10 days; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to early forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → -0.33 → 0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment phase — adjust forecast to match sentiment polarity shift 2–3 days ahead.
